# Data preparation

Audit counts report table rows and distinct non-missing participants separately;
rows in longitudinal tables are not necessarily unique participants or visits.

```{r}
data_bl_raw <- readr::read_csv(
  projr::projr_path_get("raw-data", "baseline_cohort.csv")
)
data_long_raw <- readr::read_csv(
  projr::projr_path_get("raw-data", "longitudinal_visits.csv")
)
audit_table(data_bl_raw, show_rows = FALSE)
audit_table(data_long_raw, show_rows = FALSE)
```

## Audit of raw files

### Baseline

```{r}
data_bl_raw |>
  UtilsDataRSV::view_cols()
```

Check for any subjid's not matching PT-<dddd> format:

```{r}
data_bl_raw |>
  dplyr::filter(!grepl("^PT-\\d{4}$", subjid)) |>
  audit_table()
```

There are none.

Let's check if there are any duplicate subjid's:

```{r}
data_bl_raw |>
  dplyr::group_by(subjid) |>
  dplyr::filter(dplyr::n() > 1) |>
  dplyr::ungroup() |>
  audit_table()
```

There are none.

Let's check if each person stays at the same site:

```{r}
data_bl_raw |>
  dplyr::group_by(subjid) |>
  dplyr::filter(dplyr::n_distinct(site_id) > 1) |>
  dplyr::ungroup() |>
  audit_table()
```

They all stay at the same site.

Now we can check for enrollment dates not in the yyyy-mm-dd format:

```{r}
data_bl_raw |>
  dplyr::filter(!grepl("^\\d{4}-\\d{2}-\\d{2}$", enroll_dt)) |>
  audit_table()
```

There are none.

Let's see what the range of enrolment dates is, in case anything looks odd or misspecified:

```{r}
data_bl_raw |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    min_enroll_dt = min(as.Date(enroll_dt)),
    max_enroll_dt = max(as.Date(enroll_dt))
  )
```

So, six-month enolment period looks reasonable (could check against raw docs if had time).

Let's check the ranges, IQR and typical values of `age_yrs`, `base_egfr` and `risk_score`:

```{r}
data_bl_raw |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    min_age_yrs = min(age_yrs, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_age_yrs = max(age_yrs, na.rm = TRUE),
    iqr_age_yrs = IQR(age_yrs, na.rm = TRUE),
    med_age_yrs = median(age_yrs, na.rm = TRUE),
    min_base_egfr = min(base_egfr, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_base_egfr = max(base_egfr, na.rm = TRUE),
    iqr_base_egfr = IQR(base_egfr, na.rm = TRUE),
    med_base_egfr = median(base_egfr, na.rm = TRUE),
    min_risk_score = min(risk_score, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_risk_score = max(risk_score, na.rm = TRUE),
    iqr_risk_score = IQR(risk_score, na.rm = TRUE),
    med_risk_score = median(risk_score, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) |>
  print(width = Inf)
```

So, we've got a ten year old, that seems weird.
I suppose you can take this to prevent getting HIV via non-sexual means, so I'll assume that.

I don't know what normal ranges would be for the base_egfr value, but I see at least the risk score is within correct bounds (0-10).

Okay, that looks fine. Let's convert the `enroll_dt` column to Date format, and make subjid lower case.

```{r}
data_bl_tidy <- data_bl_raw |>
  dplyr:::mutate(
    enroll_dt = as.Date(enroll_dt),
    subjid = tolower(subjid),
    site_id = tolower(site_id)
  )
```

Let's check that the range matches what we expect (correct reference date for conversion from csv):

```{r}
data_bl_tidy |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    min_enroll_dt = min(enroll_dt, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_enroll_dt = max(enroll_dt, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
```

That's correct.

Let's check sample size briefly:

```{r}
data_bl_tidy |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    n = dplyr::n(),
    n_unique_subjid = length(unique(subjid))
  )
```

So, 600.

### Longitudinal

```{r}
data_long_raw |>
  UtilsDataRSV::view_cols()
```

So, we have some NA entires in the `egfr_val` column, but none elsewhere.
We'll convert the hiv_status variable from 1 0 to "infected", "uninfected".

We'll make regimen and adh_biomarker lower case.

Okay, so, let's do the same checks for subjid:

```{r}
# Check for any subjid's not matching PT-<dddd> format
data_long_raw |>
  dplyr::filter(!grepl("^PT-\\d{4}$", subjid)) |>
  audit_table()

# Check for any duplicate subjid's
# with the same visit dates
data_long_raw |>
  dplyr::group_by(subjid, visit_dt) |>
  dplyr::filter(dplyr::n() > 1) |>
  dplyr::ungroup() |>
  audit_table()
```

Okay, so, there are 38.
Did they all only differ by regimen, so we have them recorded as both ORAL and CAB_LA?

```{r}
n_row_distinct_dupl_subjid_visit <- data_long_raw |>
  dplyr::group_by(subjid, visit_dt) |>
  dplyr::filter(dplyr::n() > 1) |>
  dplyr::ungroup() |>
  dplyr::select(-regimen) |>
  dplyr::distinct() |>
  nrow()
n_unique_subjectid_dupl_subjid_visit <- data_long_raw |>
  dplyr::group_by(subjid, visit_dt) |>
  dplyr::filter(dplyr::n() > 1) |>
  dplyr::ungroup() |>
  dplyr::distinct(subjid) |>
  nrow()
```

There are `r n_row_distinct_dupl_subjid_visit` rows with duplicate subjid and visit_dt combinations, and they involve `r n_unique_subjectid_dupl_subjid_visit` unique subjects.
So, one person remained a duplicate after removing the regimen column.
Scanning the table, that is `PT-0133` at visit `2024-10-24`.

```{r}
data_long_raw |>
  dplyr::filter(
    subjid == "PT-0133" &
    visit_dt == "2024-10-24"
  ) |>
  audit_table()
```

So, this person had two `egfr_val` readings.
I suggest we just average the two.
Can query later.

```{r}
data_long_raw_0133 <- data_long_raw |>
  dplyr::filter(
    subjid == "PT-0133" &
    visit_dt == "2024-10-24"
  ) |>
  dplyr::group_by(
    subjid, visit_dt, regimen, hiv_status, adh_biomarker
  ) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    egfr_val = mean(egfr_val, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) |>
  dplyr::ungroup()
data_long_tidy_0133 <- data_long_raw |>
  dplyr::filter(
    !(subjid == "PT-0133" &
    visit_dt == "2024-10-24")
  ) |>
  dplyr::bind_rows(data_long_raw_0133)
audit_table(data_long_tidy_0133, show_rows = FALSE)
```

Okay, let's confirm for all the others that they really did have duplicate subjid and visit_dt combinations only differing by regimen:

```{r}
data_long_tidy_0133 |>
  dplyr::group_by(subjid, visit_dt) |>
  dplyr::filter(dplyr::n() > 1) |>
  dplyr::ungroup() |>
  dplyr::group_by(subjid, visit_dt) |>
  dplyr::filter(length(unique(regimen)) == 1) |>
  dplyr::ungroup() |>
  audit_table()
```

None of these duplicate visits had only one regimen.
I am not sure whether they received both oral and cab_la regimens at the same visit, or if this is some other kind of mistake.
We exclude this visit and all subsequent visits from the analysis, unless it is their last visit, in which case the actual treatment at that point does not matter.

```{r}
data_long_tidy_dupl_reg_inc_visit <- data_long_tidy_0133 |>
  dplyr::group_by(subjid, visit_dt) |>
  dplyr::filter(dplyr::n() > 1) |>
  dplyr::ungroup() |>
  dplyr::group_by(subjid, visit_dt) |>
  dplyr::filter(length(unique(regimen)) > 1) |>
  dplyr::ungroup() |>
  dplyr::rename(visit_dt_dupl_reg = visit_dt) |>
  dplyr::select(subjid, visit_dt_dupl_reg) |>
  dplyr::distinct()
audit_table(data_long_tidy_dupl_reg_inc_visit, show_rows = FALSE)
pid_vec_dupl_reg <- data_long_tidy_dupl_reg_inc_visit |>
  dplyr::distinct(subjid) |>
  dplyr::pull(subjid)

data_long_tidy_dupl_reg_exc <- data_long_tidy_0133 |>
  dplyr::filter(!(subjid %in% pid_vec_dupl_reg))

data_long_tidy_dupl_reg <- data_long_tidy_0133 |>
  dplyr::filter(subjid %in% pid_vec_dupl_reg)

data_long_tidy_dupl_reg_inc <- data_long_tidy_dupl_reg |>
  dplyr::left_join(
    data_long_tidy_dupl_reg_inc_visit,
    by = c("subjid")
  ) |>
  dplyr::filter(
    visit_dt <= visit_dt_dupl_reg
  ) |>
  dplyr::select(-visit_dt_dupl_reg)

data_long_tidy_excluded <- data_long_tidy_dupl_reg_exc |>
  dplyr::bind_rows(data_long_tidy_dupl_reg_inc)
audit_table(data_long_tidy_excluded, show_rows = FALSE)
```

So, wrt the remaining variables, we know hiv is either 0 or 1. 
I suppose it's left a numeric vairable because that's more conveneit for surivval analysis, so we'll leave it as taht.

Let's check the range of `egfr_val` values:

```{r}
data_long_tidy_excluded |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    min_egfr = min(egfr_val, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_egfr = max(egfr_val, na.rm = TRUE),
    iqr_egft = IQR(egfr_val, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_egfr = median(egfr_val, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
```

Looks like a similar range to baseline.

Okay, let's convert the `adh_biomarker` and subjid columns to lower-case, and visit_dt to Date.

```{r}
data_long_tidy_adh <- data_long_tidy_excluded |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    adh_biomarker = tolower(adh_biomarker),
    visit_dt = as.Date(visit_dt),
    regimen = tolower(regimen),
    subjid = tolower(subjid)
  )
```

Let's remove all visits after hiv infection:

```{r}
data_long_ever_infected <- data_long_tidy_adh |>
  # get all visits
  dplyr::group_by(subjid) |>
  dplyr::mutate(ever_infected = any(hiv_status == 1)) |>
  dplyr::ungroup() |>
  dplyr::filter(ever_infected) |>
  dplyr::select(-ever_infected) |>
  dplyr::group_by(subjid) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    date_infxn = min(visit_dt[hiv_status == 1])
  ) |>
  dplyr::filter(
    visit_dt <= date_infxn
  ) |>
  dplyr::ungroup() |>
  dplyr::select(-date_infxn)

data_long_never_infected <- data_long_tidy_adh |>
  dplyr::group_by(subjid) |>
  dplyr::mutate(ever_infected = any(hiv_status == 1)) |>
  dplyr::filter(!ever_infected) |>
  dplyr::select(-ever_infected) |>
  dplyr::ungroup()

data_long_tidy_pre_infxn <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  data_long_ever_infected,
  data_long_never_infected
)
audit_table(data_long_tidy_pre_infxn, show_rows = FALSE)
```

```{r}
data_long_tidy <- data_long_tidy_pre_infxn
```

### Merging

Okay, let's merge based on `subjid`.

```{r}
data_merged <- data_bl_tidy |>
  dplyr::full_join(
    data_long_tidy,
    by = c("subjid")
  ) |>
  dplyr::select(
    subjid, enroll_dt, site_id, age_yrs, base_egfr, risk_score,
    visit_dt, regimen, adh_biomarker, egfr_val, hiv_status, dplyr::everything()
  ) |>
  dplyr::arrange(subjid, enroll_dt, visit_dt)
audit_table(data_merged, show_rows = FALSE)
```

Let's check whether we've got participants without any follow-up visits:

```{r}
data_merged_no_followup <- data_merged |>
  dplyr::group_by(subjid) |>
  dplyr::filter(all(visit_dt <= enroll_dt)) |>
  dplyr::ungroup()
audit_table(data_merged_no_followup)
```

The number of individuals is `r dplyr::n_distinct(data_merged_no_followup$subjid)`.
We exclude them, as they provide no information as to follow-up visits after enrolment.

```{r}
data_merged_with_followup <- data_merged |>
  dplyr::group_by(subjid) |>
  dplyr::filter(!all(visit_dt <= enroll_dt)) |>
  dplyr::ungroup()
audit_table(data_merged_with_followup, show_rows = FALSE)
```

Let's check that all visit dates take place after enrolment:

```{r}
# before, clearly wrong
data_merged_before_enroll <- data_merged_with_followup |>
  dplyr::filter(visit_dt < enroll_dt)
audit_table(data_merged_before_enroll)
```

So, for these `r nrow(data_merged_before_enroll)` visits, the visit date is before enrolment.
We exclude them.

```{r}
data_merged_not_before_enroll <- data_merged_with_followup |>
  dplyr::filter(visit_dt >= enroll_dt) 
audit_table(data_merged_not_before_enroll, show_rows = FALSE)
```

Let's check again if we have got follow-up visits for every participant:

```{r}
data_merged_not_before_enroll |>
  dplyr::group_by(subjid) |>
  dplyr::filter(!any(visit_dt >= enroll_dt)) |>
  dplyr::ungroup() |>
  audit_table()
```

Okay, so that's fine then.

Let's check that we've got the visits that occur exactly on the enrolment date.

```{r}
# at, needs clarification
data_merged_at_enroll <- data_merged_not_before_enroll |>
  dplyr::filter(visit_dt == enroll_dt)
audit_table(data_merged_at_enroll)
```

So, `r nrow(data_merged_at_enroll)` rows. Let's check that's everyone:

```{r}
data_merged_no_bl_long_visit <- data_merged_not_before_enroll |>
  dplyr::group_by(subjid) |>
  dplyr::filter(!any(visit_dt == enroll_dt)) |>
  dplyr::ungroup()
audit_table(data_merged_no_bl_long_visit, width = Inf)
```

So, for these `r dplyr::n_distinct(data_merged_no_bl_long_visit$subjid)` individuals, we've got no visits occurring exactly on the enrolment date.
I am not entirely sure we should exclude them (will have a better idea once we (eventually) start analysign them), but okay.
Let's just exclude them for the sake of time for now, it's only two people, and neither developed HIV, so they're not as "rare".

```{r}
data_merged_not_has_bl_long_visit <- data_merged_not_before_enroll |>
  dplyr::group_by(subjid) |>
  dplyr::filter(any(visit_dt == enroll_dt)) |>
  dplyr::ungroup()
audit_table(data_merged_not_has_bl_long_visit, show_rows = FALSE)
```

Save the table:

```{r}
data_merged_tidy <- data_merged_not_has_bl_long_visit
projr::projr_use_data(data_merged_tidy)
```

```{r}
data_merged_tidy |>
  UtilsDataRSV::view_cols()
```
